frequency_question: How often have complex executive trade enforcement actions met or beaten a sub-120-day implementation timeline when fully prioritized?
membership_rule: Includes executive actions changing tariff rates significantly on major trading partners where customs code integration is required; excludes routine tariff adjustments handled entirely by automated schedule updates.

cases.name: Liberation Day Tariffs / Emergency Economic Powers Actions

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named historical instances of fast-track executive tariff implementations; population is small because statutory bypass or emergency authorities are rarely used for 50 percent magnitude tariffs on major allies.
known_gaps: Excludes standard administrative rulemaking processes under the APA which take 6-12 months, as emergency tariff implementation typically relies on statutory exemptions (e.g., IEEPA or Section 301/232).
skeleton: Executive actions utilizing emergency trade authorities with direct Presidential mandates to Customs and Border Protection
multiplier: 3 successful rapid implementations out of 3 attempted under immediate executive order directives
validity_reason: Relies on unchanging statutory executive authorities under the Tariff Act of 1930, Trade Expansion Act of 1962, and IEEPA, valid for the duration of current administrative law frameworks.
